::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 2 [1893]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95
:::

My dear [Henry](people/person_184.qmd)
[Mr Steward](people/person_1680.qmd) has written at last. He says two very nice girls [Mildred Luckett](people/person_906.qmd) and [Kate Brown](people/person_212.qmd) will be ready at Christmas, so I am writing to him to engage one of them, and she can talk it over with [A. Diddams](people/person_1681.qmd) who can tell her all about the place.[^1]

He also gives me a list of ex pupil teachers who could keep school after the 1st of October till the mistress is ready. They all have homes near at hand and I think we can get one of them.

[Amy Bateman](people/person_783.qmd) is going to Winchester tomorrow, so I am sending her the names and asking her to enquire.

Your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The letter must date between the arrival of the Bowleses in Otterbourne in October 1892 and the marriage of Amy Jones-Bateman in August 1894.
[^2]: Mildred Luckett (b. Dalston 1871/2) and Kate H. Brown (b. Salisbury 1871/2) were both pupils at the Salisbury Diocesan Training School in 1891, learning to be teachers.
